title: auth/header: clarify project/org keys, scoped tokens, CORS, and request-signing; stabilize streaming handshake
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: The OpenAI-compat layer and our streaming endpoint have had intermittent customer confusion and a few integration bugs caused by ambiguous Authorization/header semantics (project vs org keys), missing CORS exposures for new Redwood headers, and a flaky streaming auth handshake when using request signing/nonce headers. This PR unifies and documents header behavior, adds robust handling for scoped tokens, updates CORS exposure, and stabilizes the streaming initial handshake. Changes are designed to be backward-compatible with existing Bearer tokens and OpenAI-style organization headers while enabling explicit project-scoped and org-scoped tokens and optional request-signing for higher-assurance integrations.

What this PR does (summary):
- Explicit parsing rules for Authorization values: we accept Bearer tokens (sk-*, prj-*, org-*) and canonicalize into internal token types (project, org, session).
- Introduces support for an optional scope header: "X-Redwood-Scope" (openai-compat will also accept "OpenAI-Scope" and map it). This enables short-lived scoped tokens that are narrower than full keys.
- Adds "Redwood-Request-Signature" and "Redwood-Nonce" handling for signed requests; these are optional and validated when present. For streaming websocket/http2 handshakes the nonce flow is now deterministic (server issues a challenge nonce in first response when request-signing required).
- CORS updates: Access-Control-Expose-Headers and Access-Control-Allow-Headers now include our new headers (Redwood-Request-Signature, Redwood-Nonce, X-Redwood-Scope) and continue to expose OpenAI-compatible headers (OpenAI-Organization).
- OpenAI compatibility mappings: incoming OpenAI-style headers (OpenAI-Organization, Authorization bearer patterns) are preserved and forwarded where appropriate; the compatibility layer emits guidance warnings when clients use deprecated patterns.
- Streaming stability: handshake logic refactored to ensure header validation happens before stream body processing; flaky race between auth validation and initial chunk parsing was fixed. Added retries for transient signature validation errors during handshake.
- Docs and examples: updated compatibility doc and quickstart examples to show correct headers and examples for signed requests and scope usage.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for header parsing and scope mapping
- [x] Integration tests for streaming handshake (rerun flaky test until stable)
- [x] CORS behavior validated with browser test harness
- [x] Documentation updates in /docs/openai-compat/auth.md

Migration notes for customers:
- Existing Bearer tokens continue to work without changes.
- If you use organization-scoped workflows via OpenAI-Organization, no immediate action is required; we forward the header.
- For customers adopting scoped tokens or request-signing: follow docs/openai-compat/auth.md for token formats and ephemeral token exchange flow.

Rollout: feature gated behind compatibility flag 'compat/auth-header-v2' for two-week canary, then enabled globally. Backwards-compatible fallback enabled: if a request fails strict validation and is from a known legacy client-agent, we fall back to permissive parse mode and emit a deprecation metric.

reviews: Raj Patel (review): Found one edge case parsing 'Bearer prj-' when additional whitespace present; suggested trim and robust split - addressed in commit a1d2c3e.
Elena Gomez (review): Requested explicit behavior for OpenAI-Organization forwarding; added mapping and tests (commit e3n4o5p).

ci_checks: integration-tests: streaming-handshake: flaky (initial run failed), rerun -> pass
release_notes: Clarified Authorization and header semantics for project/org keys and scoped tokens. Added optional request-signing (Redwood-Request-Signature/Redwood-Nonce) and updated CORS exposures. Streaming handshake auth validation made deterministic and more robust. Backwards compatible; see docs/openai-compat/auth.md for migration steps.
security_impact: Tightened validation of request-signatures and explicit scoping reduces risk of token abuse. No new privileged endpoints introduced. Audit logs will include scope and signature validation results.
testing: Added unit tests for parser edge cases, integration test for streaming handshake (rerun until stable), and browser harness to validate CORS exposures. Manual verification with Postman and internal client simulator performed.
rollout_plan: Enable behind 'compat/auth-header-v2' flag. Canaries on 10% traffic for 7 days, monitor auth.failures, signature.failures, and compat.deprecation metrics. If stable, flip global flag and remove legacy permissive fallback after 30 days with deprecation notice.
notes: This PR touches compatibility behavior; please coordinate with SDK teams (redwood-sdk-python/redwood-sdk-typescript) to publish client examples. We added deprecation metrics to help identify legacy clients.
